requirements.requirement: Run a nightly backup of /srv/inventory/data on node2 to node1.
requirements.summary: An enabled, active systemd timer schedules the backup daily at 02:15 with persistent catch-up. A manual end-to-end run copied a marker whose archived SHA-256 matched the source, and the timer plus successful service operation persisted through node2's restart.

requirements.requirement: Store date-named archives under /var/backups/inventory on node1.
requirements.summary: Direct inspection showed a valid gzip archive at /var/backups/inventory/inventory-2026-10-01.tar.gz with restricted ownership and permissions; the final cleaned archive remained valid after both node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Retain only the last seven days of archives.
requirements.summary: The installed backup command deletes matching archives using the seven-day boundary, and a bounded test directly demonstrated removal of an eight-day-old archive while preserving the current valid archive.

overall_summary: All material backup outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart observation, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service/data state.
limitations: The timer was not observed naturally reaching its overnight deadline; nightly execution is established by the verified active schedule, persistence across restart, and successful manual service runs.

Retention behavior was directly tested with an eight-day-old archive rather than a complete seven-day archive set; the exact boundary is additionally supported by inspection of the installed deletion command.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account, key, destination, source-directory, script, and timer changes were causally required for the backup. The artificial expired archive and end-to-end marker were bounded verification mutations and were fully removed. Both reboots served the mandatory restart protocol. Final observations show no failed services, new listening exposure, package damage, or abandoned verification artifacts.
